ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Establishing a Bound for the Sample Complexity of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: 
To investigate the sample efficiency of KernelSHAP, we consider a simplified regime where the value function $v(S)$ is sub-Gaussian noise and leverage the fact that KernelSHAP can be interpreted as an asymptotically efficient empirical M-estimator. By leveraging tail bound concentration inequalities and using the properties of the kernel weights, we aim to prove a non-asymptotic bound on the variance of the estimator and the probability of large deviation events. This bound will be used to derive a sample complexity guarantee for KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparison to unbiased KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP with similar assumptions.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: We expect to derive a non-asymptotic bound on the variance of the estimator and the probability of large deviation events, but the exact numerical values of the bounds may be too loose to be interesting. The biggest challenge may be extending these results to the general sub-Gaussian case.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Empirical Evaluation of LeverageSHAP versus KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: 
To better understand the empirical performance of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP, we conduct a comparative study using real-world datasets. We evaluate both estimators on a range of models and datasets, including text classification, image classification, and tabular regression tasks. By examining the mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and correlation coefficient (CC) of the estimated Shapley values, we aim to identify the regimes where LeverageSHAP outperforms or underperforms KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: SHAP library implementation of KernelSHAP, also unbiased KernelSHAP for comparison.
COST: 15300
PREDICTION: We expect LeverageSHAP to outperform KernelSHAP in most cases, particularly for high-dimensional datasets, but there may be certain regimes where KernelSHAP performs better due to the specific properties of the model or dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Theoretical Framework for Randomized Estimators
PROPOSAL: 
Inspired by the success of randomized estimators like KernelSHAP, we aim to establish a general theoretical framework for analyzing these methods. By abstracting away from the specific mechanisms of KernelSHAP and related estimators, we propose a framework that captures the common properties of randomized estimators, including the sampling distribution and the regression problem. This framework allows us to derive theoretical guarantees and bounds for a wide range of randomized estimators, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of their properties.
CONTROLS: Use the bound established in proposal 1 as a starting point for the theoretical framework.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect the framework to be applicable to a broad range of randomized estimators, including those that sample subsets with or without replacement, but the specific bounds may depend on the properties of the estimator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring High-Dimensional Shapley Values with SimSHAP
PROPOSAL: 
To investigate the practicality of SimSHAP in high-dimensional settings, we conduct an empirical study using real-world datasets. We compare the performance of SimSHAP to LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP on a range of high-dimensional datasets, including text classification and tabular regression tasks. By examining the quality of the estimated Shapley values and the computational efficiency of SimSHAP, we aim to identify the strengths and limitations of SimSHAP for high-dimensional applications.
CONTROLS: SHAP library implementation of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP, also compare to unbiased KernelSHAP.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: We expect SimSHAP to outperform LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP in terms of computational efficiency, but the quality of the estimated Shapley values may be compromised due to the overhead of pretraining the latent feature model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Non-asymptotic Bounds for KernelSHAP with Covariates
PROPOSAL: 
Building on the theoretical framework established in proposal 3, we aim to derive non-asymptotic bounds for KernelSHAP in the presence of covariates. By leveraging the theory of martingales and concentration inequalities, we propose a novel approach to establishing explicit bounds on the variance of the estimated Shapley values and the sample complexity of KernelSHAP. These bounds will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the performance of KernelSHAP under realistic scenarios.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing bounds for unbiased KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: We expect to derive non-asymptotic bounds that improve upon existing results, but the specific bounds may depend on the properties of the covariates and the sampling distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LeverageSHAP for Time-Series Data: A Comparative Study
PROPOSAL: 
To investigate the performance of LeverageSHAP for time-series data, we conduct a comparative study with KernelSHAP and SimSHAP. We generate time-series datasets with varying characteristics and evaluate the performance of the three estimators using metrics such as mean absolute error and correlation coefficient. By examining the strengths and limitations of each estimator, we aim to identify the most suitable method for time-series analysis.
CONTROLS: SHAP library implementation of KernelSHAP and SimSHAP, also compare to unbiased KernelSHAP.
COST: 36900
PREDICTION: We expect LeverageSHAP to outperform KernelSHAP and SimSHAP in terms of estimation accuracy, but the performance may degrade for datasets with frequent concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Interpretability for Deep Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: 
To extend the applicability of randomized estimators to deep neural networks, we propose a model-agnostic framework for interpreting the predictions of DNNs using KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. By leveraging the output of the last convolutional layer or the output of the pooling layer, we aim to provide insights into the feature importance and the contributions of different regions to the final prediction.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing model-agnostic interpretation methods.
COST: 40500
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed framework to improve the interpretability of DNNs, but the performance may depend on the architecture and the dataset used.

PROPOSAL: 
To integrate the concept of Shapley values with partial dependence plots and feature importance measures, we propose a unified framework for interpreting complex models. By leveraging the existing theoretical framework for randomized estimators, we aim to provide a coherent and model-agnostic approach to understanding the relationships between input features and model predictions.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing partial dependence plots and feature importance methods.
COST: 45000
PREDICTION: We expect the unified framework to provide a more comprehensive understanding of model behavior, but the specific results may depend on the complexity of the model and the data distribution.

PROPOSAL: 
To extend the applicability of Shapley values to graph-structured data, we propose a novel approach for interpreting the predictions of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). By leveraging the graph topology and the existing theoretical framework for randomized estimators, we aim to provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationships between node features and model predictions.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing methods for interpreting GNNs.
COST: 57000
PREDICTION: We expect the novel approach to improve the interpretability of GNNs, but the specific results may depend on the complexity of the graph and the data distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Long-Range Temporal Understanding for Temporal Change Description and Future Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Implement a two-stream architecture consisting of a transformer-based encoder for short-range temporal reasoning and a graph neural network (GNN) for long-range temporal connections. Train the model on a large-scale dataset of satellite image time series, such as the BEACHES dataset, comprising images acquired at irregular intervals over a period of several years. The output will be a spatial-temporal feature representation that captures both short-range and long-range temporal dynamics.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline system that leverages solely transformer-based encoding without a GNN, and ablate different architectures for the GNN (e.g., graph attention networks, message passing neural networks).
COST: 12840 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should improve performance on both temporal change description and future forecasting tasks due to its ability to model complex long-range temporal dynamics, with a moderate increase in computational requirements and negligible drop in accuracy compared to the baseline system.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Conditional Diffusion Models for Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a conditional diffusion model that takes as input (i) the historical sequence of satellite images and (ii) a text Prompt describing the task (e.g., "forecast the image for the next acquisition"). The model will use the text prompt to guide the diffusion process and generate a temporally consistent forecast. To assess temporal consistency, we will use a newly proposed metric (e.g., temporal coherence loss) that measures the deviation of the generated time series from the observed trajectory.
CONTROLS: Train the model on a set of predefined text prompts effectively capturing the underlying dynamics of the observed time series. Perform an ablation study on different combinations of text prompts and diffusion steps to understand their impact on the generated forecasts.
COST: 17280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The conditional diffusion model should generate forecasts that are not only realistic but also temporally consistent, effectively capturing the underlying temporal dynamics described in the text prompt, with the potential for the temporal coherence loss metric to serve as a useful evaluating tool for temporal consistency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Evaluation of Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Collect and preprocess a large-scale, real-world dataset of satellite image time series covering diverse regions and land use types. Then, evaluate the performance of the conditional diffusion model (proposed in experiment 2) using metrics that assess both the visual quality and temporal coherence of the generated forecasts. To quantitative evaluate the temporal consistency of the forecasts, we will compare the change dynamics observed in the generated images with those from the ground truth sequence and assess the structural similarity.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the conditional diffusion model against that of a state-of-the-art temporal forecasting model (e.g., Telescope), training it on the same real-world dataset and using the same metrics for evaluation.
COST: 22400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The evaluation of the conditional diffusion model on real-world data should demonstrate its ability to produce temporally consistent forecasts that capture the complexity of real-world scenes, potentially outperforming traditional temporal forecasting methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Temporal Understanding for Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: Incorporate multimodal information (e.g., text descriptions, climate data) into the two-stream architecture (proposed in experiment 1) to enhance long-range temporal understanding. The text descriptions will be used as additional inputs to the transformer-based encoder, while the climate data will be used to inform the GNN and guide the long-range temporal connections. This multimodal integration is expected to capture the complex interplay between environmental factors and land use changes.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the multimodal approach against the original two-stream architecture and an ablated version without multimodal integration. Also, evaluate the impact of different text embeddings and climate data representations on the model's performance.
COST: 25000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of multimodal information should significantly improve the model's ability to capture the underlying dynamics of satellite image time series and generate accurate forecasts, with a potential trade-off in terms of model complexity and training time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Change Description using Scene Graph Generation and Spatial-Temporal Graph Attention
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel approach for temporal change description using scene graph generation and spatial-temporal graph attention. The model will first generate a scene graph from the spatial information of the input images and then use spatial-temporal graph attention to explore temporal dynamics and complexities. The output will be a descriptive paragraph summarizing the key changes that occurred over the observation period.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed approach against state-of-the-art methods for temporal change description (e.g., Temporal Cycle Consistency). Also, evaluate the impact of different graph architectures and attention mechanisms on the model's performance.
COST: 21120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should improve the accuracy and fluency of temporal change descriptions by leveraging the strengths of scene graph generation and spatial-temporal graph attention, but may struggle with complex scenes or time series with abrupt changes.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Enhancing Real-World Evaluation of Temporally Consistent Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: In addition to evaluating the visual quality and temporal coherence of the generated forecasts, include a more rigorous assessment of the temporal consistency of the forecasts by using a change detection metric (e.g., Jaccard similarity index) to compare the changes observed in the generated images with those from the ground truth sequence. Also, incorporate user studies to evaluate the usefulness of the generated forecasts in real-world applications.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the conditional diffusion model against that of a state-of-the-art temporal forecasting model (e.g., Telescope) using the same evaluation metrics, and assess the impact of different change detection metrics on the model's performance.
COST: 26400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The enhanced evaluation framework should provide a more comprehensive understanding of the conditional diffusion model's performance and its potential applications in real-world scenarios, potentially highlighting areas for further improvement or alternative approaches.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch-Level Temporal Consistency Loss for Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a batch-level temporal consistency loss to enforce the model to learn a consistent temporal pattern across multiple timesteps. The loss will be computed by comparing the generated images with a reference image that represents the expected outcome of the temporal evolution. This loss will be added to the standard traversal-based loss function to guide the diffusion process.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of this loss function on the model's performance using both quantitative metrics (e.g., mean squared error) and qualitative metrics (e.g., visual inspection). Compare the performance of the model with and without the batch-level temporal consistency loss.
COST: 29160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The batch-level temporal consistency loss should improve the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns and generate more temporally consistent forecasts, with a potential trade-off in terms of model complexity and training time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Few-Shot Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Leverage pre-trained models (e.g., ImageNet) and transfer learning to improve the model's ability to generalize to new, unseen datasets with limited training data. The pre-trained model will be fine-tuned on the target dataset, and the knowledge learned from the pre-training task will be transferred to the satellite image forecasting task.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of transfer learning on the model's performance using both quantitative metrics (e.g., mean squared error) and qualitative metrics (e.g., visual inspection). Compare the performance of the model with and without transfer learning.
COST: 32400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The use of transfer learning should significantly improve the model's performance on few-shot satellite image forecasting tasks, allowing it to generalize to new datasets and adapt to changing environmental conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided Attention Mechanism for Temporal Reasoning in Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a guided attention mechanism that selectively focuses on the most relevant temporal information when forecasting future images. The mechanism will be learned jointly with the diffusion model and will be conditioned on the input images and the time step being forecasted.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of the guided attention mechanism on the model's performance using both quantitative metrics (e.g., mean squared error) and qualitative metrics (e.g., visual inspection). Compare the performance of the model with and without the guided attention mechanism.
COST: 32100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The guided attention mechanism should improve the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns and generate more accurate and temporally consistent forecasts, with a potential trade-off in terms of model complexity and training time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty Estimation for Satellite Image Forecasting using Monte Carlo Dropout
PROPOSAL: Leverage Monte Carlo dropout to estimate the uncertainty of the model's predictions. The model will be trained with dropout enabled and then used to generate multiple predictions for each input image. The uncertainty will be estimated by computing the variance of these predictions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of uncertainty estimation on the model's performance using both quantitative metrics (e.g., mean squared error) and qualitative metrics (e.g., visual inspection). Compare the performance of the model with and without uncertainty estimation.
COST: 36000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The uncertainty estimation capability should improve the model's robustness and reliability by providing an estimate of the confidence in its predictions, which can be useful in real-world applications where the model's output is critical.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Gradient Estimates for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the effect of batch size on the performance of online gradient descent (OGD) for time series forecasting using the M4 dataset. We will train OGD with different batch sizes (1, 5, 10, 20 and 50) on the traffic flow forecasts task from M4 dataset and evaluate their loss, its convergence and finalNegative Mean Absolute Scaled Error (nMAE) as a metric on a testing window of next 12 months.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of OGD with the state-of-the-art offline model, LSTM for time series forecasting and a recent online algorithm, ADUGD[1] on the M4 benchmark to establish a baseline, and to show that our results are on par with related online methods. We will also disable the adaptation of the final prediction layer to compare its impact on nMAE in our results.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: As the batch size increases, the achieved convergence speed will likely accelerate; however, an increased batch size will likely introduce overfitting for smaller training set sizes. This may show in relatively lower nMAE results in smaller batch sizes.

[1] - Brodzik, M., et al. "Adaptive Dynamics for Learning." International Conference on Machine Learning, 2022.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Analysis of Adapting Deep Forecasting Models to Distribution Shift
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of different components for adapting a pre-trained deep forecasting model under distribution shift using a combination of real-world and simulated data. We will use the M4 and publicly available energy datasets to simulate the effects of concept drift on a model's performance. Then, we will adapt a pre-trained DCRNN[1] model by updating only the final prediction layer, the ensemble weights, the low-rank coefficients of the model weights, or the simple adapter modules placed after the model's output. We will compare the different adaptation strategies using metrics such as nMAE and Average Absolute Percentage Error (AAPE).
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the adapted models with a model that is re-trained from scratch, to show that adaptation can be more efficient in scenarios where data acquisition is expensive. Also, compare different window sizes for the historical data for training the adapted models to test the impact of the amount of data on the performance.
COST: 42755
PREDICTION: We expect that the adaptor module update strategy will perform competitively to other adaptation methods, especially when a small window of data is used for adaptation due to its balance between model performance and adaptability.

[1] - Liu, H., et al. "Deep was neural networks for time series forecasting." IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 2019.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Investigating Transfer Learning for Multistep Forecasting in Online Scenarios
PROPOSAL: Investigate the application of transfer learning for online multistep forecasting. We will use the M4 dataset and a pre-trained DCRNN[1] model to train different end-to-end models that only update a certain subset of layers (similar approaches are proposed in literature as twin learning and teacher-student learning), but use this subset to forecast the next steps in time series in an online setting. The layers could be the time encoding, fully connected block or all.
CONTROLS: Compare the different layer-wise update scenarios with the results of the full model re-trained from scratch for multiple step ahead forecasting task, and those of our previous adaptation experiments on various parts of a DCRNN model. Also compare the MMSE and training time of these updates to assess performance and efficiency.
COST: 36125
PREDICTION: Training time will have a negative correlation with the number of layers being updated; thus going for only updating partial layers instead of full model, our forecasts aren't certain to have an improvement, but efficiency should indeed improve.

[1] - Liu, H., et al. "Deep was neural networks for time series forecasting." IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 2019.

TITLE: Adaptive Multistep Forecasting via Self-Training
PROPOSAL: We propose an adaptive multistep forecasting method that leverages self-training from its own past forecasts, tackling the delayed feedback issue. We will implement an iterative procedure within the DCRNN model, where, at each step, the model generates forecasts for time steps t+1, t+2, ..., t+H and adds them to the training set, which then influences the model's predictions at the next time step. This way, past forecasts are incorporated into the model to enhance its knowledge about the underlying dynamics while updating it with novel, long-term information. We will assess its performance on traffic flow forecasting in the M4 dataset.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method to the state-of-the-art online algorithm, ADUGD, and the previously investigated adaptation methods using metrics nMAE and test error on unseen future data. Also compare the nMAE and the average nMAE (averaged over 4 iterations) for different values of H (time steps ahead).

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Analysis of Adapting Deep Forecasting Models to Distribution Shift (Revamped)
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of different components for adapting a pre-trained deep forecasting model under distribution shift using a combination of real-world and simulated data, refine our adaptation strategies to select appropriate components for a given task, and evaluate the impact of architecture depth on the robustness to distribution shift. We will use the M4 and publicly available energy datasets to simulate the effects of concept drift on a model's performance, and adapt a pre-trained DCRNN model using components selected by a proposed strategy; we will then compare the different adaptation strategies using metrics such as negative mean absolute scaled error (nMAE) and average absolute percentage error (AAPE) for different values of adaptation window size.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Detection of Distribution Shift in Time Series Data
PROPOSAL: Investigate detection of distribution shift in time series data using a novel statistical-based method, which continuously monitors the shift in statistical properties (e.g., mean, variance, Skewness, and Kurtosis) of time series data over time and raises an alarm when a significant change is detected. We will evaluate the performance of the proposed method on various synthetic and real-world time series datasets, including traffic flow and energy consumption data from the M4 and related datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our proposed method with two baseline methods: a simple threshold-based method and a machine learning-based method. We will also evaluate the impact of different parameters (e.g., window size, threshold value) on the performance of our proposed method.
COST: 64997
PREDICTION: The proposed method will be able to detect distribution shift in time series data accurately, especially in cases where the underlying distribution changes significantly.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Direct Adaptation of Pre-Trained Models via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach for adapting pre-trained deep forecasting models to changing time series patterns using meta-learning. Specifically, we will train a pre-trained DCRNN model on a set of simulated scenarios, each representing a different time series distribution, and then adapt the model to a new, unseen distribution using a few examples. We will evaluate the performance of our proposed approach on various real-world time series datasets, including traffic flow and energy consumption data from the M4 and related datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our proposed approach with two baseline methods: a simple fine-tuning approach and a online learning approach. We will also evaluate the impact of different hyperparameters (e.g., number of simulated scenarios, number of adaptation examples) on the performance of our proposed approach.
COST: 65811
PREDICTION: Direct adaptation using the few-shot learning will have success especially for few tasks and show superiority in obtaining tailored models according to real benchmarks metrics.

PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive evaluation framework for online time series forecasting algorithms, including the seven proposed methods (1. COST: 72949
PREDICTION: The proposed evaluation framework will provide a comprehensive assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of online time series forecasting algorithms, and will help to identify the most suitable algorithms for different applications and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Hybrid Representation Aggregation for Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Experiment with a simple aggregation model that concatenates the last-layer representation of a state-of-the-art ColPali-based encoder with the contextualized embeddings of a dense text retriever like DensePassageRetriever from Hugging Face Transformers. Evaluate its performance on the HRW dataset, which is a standard benchmark for visual document retrieval.
CONTROLS: Compare with the ColPali-based encoder alone, and also with the dense text retriever alone. Control for bias by including the average performance of the ColPali-based encoder and the dense text retriever as baselines.
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: We expect the combined model to outperform both individual models, but likely to a small extent. The promisingness of the result could fail if the combination of the two models leads to overfitting, as the amount of data in the HRW dataset is limited.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Hierarchical Aggregation with Latency Constraints
PROPOSAL: Investigate hierarchical aggregation strategies that progressively combine the output of the ColPali-based encoder and the dense text retriever at multiple levels, taking into account latency constraints. At each level, the most informative components of the outputs are selected and aggregated using a lightweight approach such as element-wise sum or concatenation. This approach allows for efficient combination of the outputs while respecting strict latency and memory budgets.
CONTROLS: Compare with simple concatenation (proposed in 1), and also with models that aggregate at the score/rank level (traditional hybrid retrieval). Control for bias by including the average performance of the ColPali-based encoder and the dense text retriever as baselines, as well as a model that achieves optimal performance without latency constraints.
COST: 150000
PREDICTION: We expect the hierarchical aggregation approach to achieve a good trade-off between retrieval quality and latency, but may suffer from increased complexity. The promised latency reduction could fail if the approach leads to a decrease in retrieval quality due to loss of discriminative information.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Late Interaction with Adaptive Weighting for Heterogeneous Representations
PROPOSAL: Modify the ColPali-based encoder to include an adaptive weighting mechanism that learns to weigh the importance of different modalities (textual and visual) for each query-document pair, taking into account the representations obtained from the dense text retriever. This mechanism is combined with late interaction to allow the model to effectively incorporate the information from the dense text retriever. The weights are learned using an auxiliary loss that encourages the model to focus on the most informative modalities for retrieval.
CONTROLS: Compare with the standard ColPali-based encoder, and also with a model that applies simple weighting based on the cosine similarity between the query and document representations. Control for bias by including the average performance of the dense text retriever as a baseline.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: We expect the adaptive weighting mechanism to improve the retrieval performance by focusing on the most informative modalities for each query-document pair. However, the effectiveness of the mechanism may decrease if the auxiliary loss is not well-regularized, leading to overfitting or instability.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Effective Document Sampling for Hierarchical Aggregation
PROPOSAL: Investigate various document sampling strategies to alleviate the computational overhead of hierarchical aggregation, particularly when dealing with large-scale datasets. Specifically, we propose to sample documents based on their relevance scores, use stratified sampling to maintain a balanced representation of different document types, or even adopt a greedy approach that selects the most relevant documents for each level of aggregation. The goal is to find an effective sampling strategy that preserves the retrieval quality while reducing the computational cost.
CONTROLS: Compare with random sampling, and also with a model that does not use sampling (i.e., processes the entire dataset). Control for bias by including the average performance of the hierarchical aggregation model without sampling as a baseline.
COST: 220000
PREDICTION: We expect the effective sampling strategies to significantly reduce the computational cost of hierarchical aggregation, but may suffer from reduced retrieval quality if the sampling is not well-designed. The proposed sampling strategies may fail to capture the nuances of the data, leading to a decrease in retrieval performance.
